newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CENTRAL BANK NOT PLANNING SECURED LOANS HIKE.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CENTRAL BANK NOT PLANNING SECURED LOANS HIKE.

text.p: AMSTERDAM, Feb 27 (REUTER) - The Dutch central bank said on Thursday it was not planning to raise the secured loans rate for the time being.
Asked if there were likely to be any changes in the secured loans rate for the time being, following today's 20 basis point rise in the special advances rate, a bank spokesman said: "No."
The spokesman said the rate increase was a response to recent rises in Dutch money markets rates.
"The market had expected this to some extent...market rates had already risen somewhat and we are following that," he said.
But the move was not prompted by recent weakness of the guilder against the German mark, he said.
The special advances rate is roughly equivalent to Germany's repo rate and is the benchmark for all Dutch money market rates. It had previously been pegged at 2.50 percent since August.
The secured loans rate is roughly equivalent to Germany's discount rate and is used by commercial banks as a benchmark for their long-term loans to customers.
The secured loans rate has been pegged at 2.00 percent since April, 1996.
The central bank spokesman said the gap of 70 basis points between the special advances and secured loans rates was wide, but not exceptional.

Asked why the bank had raised the rate by 20 basis points instead of the widely expected 10 basis points, he said: "If you raise it by 10 you might have to add another 10 later, so you might as well make it 20."
After the rate hike the guilder was virtually unchanged against the mark at 112.42 per 100 marks versus 112.415 earlier.
